html:
The Tukano, who call themselves Ye'pâ-masa, are an Eastern Tukanoan people of the Vaupés River basin on the border of Colombia and Brazil. They live in riverside communities, fishing and growing bitter manioc.

The Vaupés peoples follow a rule called linguistic exogamy: a person must marry someone from a group that speaks another language. Neighbours such as the Wanano, Tuyuka and Desana each keep their own language, and many people speak several. Tukano became the common language of the region, helped by Catholic missions in the 1900s. Around 1900 rubber traders of the rubber boom forced many Vaupés men into labour. Tukano is now an official language of the municipality of São Gabriel da Cachoeira in Brazil, with Nheengatu and Baniwa.
